name: Furnish Mode
description: The buy-and-decorate editing mode for a home: a modal state where the catalog is open, the grid is visible, and clicks place or move furniture instead of driving the live sim. Mode separation is the point — a click that might buy a sofa must never also tell the sim to walk, so entering furnish mode suspends live-mode input routing and restores it on exit. This component owns mode state, the furniture catalog, and purchase validation; it does not own the placed result. housing.home_system remains the authority on plot state and saved furniture — furnish_mode requests placements and purchases, and home_system accepts or rejects them, which means build-mode exploits funnel through the same authority as every other placement. Economy is similarly delegated: furnishing costs are validated against economy.currency and paid by it, never by this component's own ledger.

inputs.name: furnitureCatalog
inputs.description: Placeable definitions: id, footprint in tiles, price, comfort/need tags, and unlock requirements. Need tags are what let furnishings fulfill social.needs_decay motives, tying decoration to gameplay.

inputs.name: sellbackFraction
inputs.description: Fraction of price returned when selling placed furniture. The 20% depreciation is genre tradition: it makes redecorating a decision, not a free shuffle.

inputs.name: allowOverlap
inputs.description: Whether footprints may overlap. False is the honest default; true is for decorative clutter layers where collision would be pedantic.

outputs.name: isActive
outputs.description: Whether furnish mode is currently entered. Live-mode systems should read this (or listen to the mode events) to suspend their input routing.

outputs.name: ghostPlacement
outputs.description: The item currently under the cursor with validity and rotation, so the renderer can draw the green/red ghost without re-deriving validity.
